## Summary

Test-first: unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` for (a) lease maintenance during the cooldown pause, (b) the cooldown-exit renewal hook, and (c) per-tick `leaderState` re-derivation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] While a leader is paused in the no-candidate cooldown, the lease file mtime/content keeps advancing (refresh continues during the pause).
- [ ] On cooldown exit, the lease is renewed BEFORE any dispatch decision (belt: even if tick loop stalled mid-pause).
- [ ] `leaderState` is re-derived every tick: an expired lease while `leaderState === true` routes into the election/takeover path instead of zombie dispatch.
- [ ] Non-leader with a valid lease held by another live instance stays silent (existing AC3 behavior preserved — regression guard).
- [ ] Tests FAIL on current code (the gaps below) and PASS after the F5 implementation.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the existing 'No-candidate cooldown (createDowntimeWorker)' describe block with a coordination-dir worker.
- Fake-timer scenarios asserting lease mtime advance during pause, renewal on exit, and re-routing on re-derived expiry.

## Dependencies

- Prereq for F5 (red → green).

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (new test cases).

## Summary

Test-first: unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.test.ts` proving `refreshLease()` renews an owned-but-expired lease (instead of no-oping) and never renews a foreign lease.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `refreshLease()` on a lease owned by this instance (`leaderId === instanceId`) but EXPIRED rewrites the lease with a fresh `acquiredAt` — no silent no-op.
- [ ] `refreshLease()` on a lease owned by ANOTHER instance stays a no-op (never steals leadership / renews a foreign lease).
- [ ] Fail-safe preserved: missing/unreadable lease file → `refreshLease()` no-op (treated as not-leader).
- [ ] Tests FAIL on current code (guarded `if (!this.isLeader()) return`) and PASS after the F4 implementation.

## Minimal Implementation

- Reuse the existing `makeManager` helper; seed a stale owned lease (write lease file with expired `acquiredAt`), call `refreshLease()`, assert the file's `acquiredAt` advanced.
- Foreign-lease no-op: seed a lease with a different `leaderId`, assert content unchanged after `refreshLease()`.

## Dependencies

- Prereq for F4 (red → green).

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.test.ts` (new test cases).

## Summary

Test-first: add a fake-timer dual-instance integration test in `packages/herdr/src/integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts` proving the zombie-in-cooldown scenario can never double-dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Leader A enters the no-candidate cooldown; its lease expires mid-pause (simulate TTL < cooldown / frozen lease file).
- [ ] Instance B detects the stale lease, wins a fresh election → exactly one instance (B) is leader.
- [ ] Zombie A must NOT dispatch (stays silent or is re-elected); across both instances `spawnAgentPane` is called at most once per coordination entry — proving no double dispatch.
- [ ] Test FAILS on current code (reproduces the bug) and PASSES after the F5 implementation.

## Minimal Implementation

- Reuse existing `makeWorker`/`baseDeps`/`idlePayload` fixtures and the shared `sharedCoord` dir.
- Scenario: A elected leader → no-candidate cooldown entered → freeze/expire A's lease mid-pause → B tick detects stale → B wins election → advance past cooldown → A tick: assert A does not dispatch while B dispatches.
- Assert `depsA.spawnAgentPane` call count === 0 (or === 1 for a re-elected A, never both instances dispatching the same entry).

## Dependencies

- Prereq for F5 (regression red → green).

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts` (new test case).

data.description:
## Summary

`refreshLease()` currently guards `if (!this.isLeader()) return`; `isLeader()` requires `isLeaseValid` (>10 s remaining). An owned-but-EXPIRED lease therefore makes `refreshLease()` silently no-op forever — the zombie can never renew. Change the guard from 'valid leader' to 'owner of the lease': renew whenever `lease.leaderId === instanceId`, regardless of current validity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `refreshLease()` renews when the lease is owned by this instance (`leaderId === instanceId`) even if expired — writes a fresh `acquiredAt` with the same TTL.
- [ ] `refreshLease()` remains a no-op when the lease is owned by another instance (never renews/stops a foreign lease; takeover-race safe).
- [ ] `refreshLease()` remains a no-op when the lease file is missing or unreadable (fail-safe: not leader).
- [ ] `isLeader()` semantics unchanged for claim/election paths (still requires a valid lease).
- [ ] Existing `leader-election.test.ts` suite passes; new self-heal tests (F3) pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `refreshLease()`: read the lease; if it exists AND `lease.leaderId === instanceId`, write a fresh lease (`acquiredAt: new Date().toISOString()`, same `ttlSeconds`). All other cases return early.
- Keep `isLeader()` / `isLeaseValid` as-is for the claim path.

## Dependencies

- F3 (unit tests) written first; green after this change.

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` (refreshLease self-heal).
data.title: Self-healing refreshLease() in leader-election.ts

data.description:
## Summary

In `tick()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`), `leaderState` is cached once at worker creation and only re-derived in an unreachable-while-leader takeover branch — an expired lease while `leaderState === true` leaves the worker dispatching as a zombie. Re-derive `leaderState` EVERY tick and add an explicit lease-renewal + re-derivation hook on cooldown exit (before any dispatch decision on resume).

CRITICAL interaction (found in plan review): `detectStaleLeader()` returns `false` for our OWN lease, so per-tick re-derivation alone would fall through BOTH the leader branch (leaderState=false) AND the takeover branch (hasLease=true, detectStaleLeader=false) — the self-heal (F4) would be starved. The leader branch must treat an owned-but-expired lease as refreshable, ensuring the self-heal is reachable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `leaderState` re-derived every tick (single cheap lease-file read) — a lease that expired mid-pause routes the worker OUT of zombie dispatch.
- [ ] Owned-but-expired lease in the leader block: `refreshLease()` (self-heal, F4) is invoked so the lease renews — never silently ignored.
- [ ] Cooldown-exit hook: when `cooldownUntil` expires, renew the lease (if leader) and re-derive leadership BEFORE any poll/dispatch decision — belt-and-braces even when the tick loop stalled mid-pause.
- [ ] Takeover-race guard: if ANOTHER instance won the lease during the pause, the re-derived state yields (worker stays silent) — never fights the new leader, never double-dispatch.
- [ ] Non-leader with a valid foreign lease stays silent (existing behavior preserved).
- [ ] Fail-safe preserved: missing/unreadable lease ⇒ treated as not leader.
- [ ] All existing unit + integration tests pass; F1/F2 regression tests (zombie, cooldown) pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Replace cached `let leaderState = ...` with per-tick `const leaderState = leaderManager ? leaderManager.isLeader() : true` (or re-derive at the top of the leader block each tick).
- In the leader block: `if (leaderState)` refresh OR `if (owned lease)` refresh-self-heal; keep takeover branch for foreign/stale/no-lease.
- In the cooldown-expiry branch (currently `cooldownUntil = null; errorStrikes = 0;`): before resuming, renew lease when owner, re-derive leadership, and if no longer leader stay silent this tick.

## Dependencies

- F1/F2 (red regression tests) and F4 (self-heal); green after this change.

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (tick() leader block + cooldown-exit hook).
